description_en: This Phalcā is located to the north of Lũ Hiti (LAL1860) in Nugaḥ Ṭola (Sundhara). After it was dismantled in 1979 CE (VS 2036), it was turned into  an elevated platform. Some residents refer to the site as an elevated open platform (ḍabalī).With exquisitely-carved windows and an interesting legend of the deity enshrined on the ground floor, the former Sataḥ (sattal) was popularly related to the Pvāḥsyāḥdyaḥ (potbellied deity), the enshrined deity for stomach ache. The deity was said to be a Sarvabhakṣa: “the one who can digest everything”. People from distant villages of the Kathmandu Valley used to come and sit here to cure their stomach pains. The two-storey Phalcā faced west and its roof was tiled withjhĩgaṭībricks. A peacock window was installed on its eastern wall. It had three bays, and the western bay was rented out to a small shop. A statue of Pvāḥsyāḥdyaḥ was said to have been stolen. A guthi of Cipālu (Shrestha) looked after the site.Local folklore says that there used to be a "beast" - not a demon - who comes out at night to drink water from the central spout with both of his hands resting on the spouts on either sides and legs on the phalcā. (member of the Nugaḥ Lũhiti Ṭola Sudhāra Samiti in conversation with Brosius and Shakya, 19.3.2024).
description_ne: नुग: टोलमा रहेको लुँ हिति (LAL1860) को उत्तरमा यो फल्चा रहेको थियो । अहिले यहाँ फल्चा छैन, फल्चा भत्केपछि अवशेषको रूपमा भुइँतलाको पेटी मात्र बाँकी छ । यसलाई अहिले डबलीको रूपमा प्रयोग गरिन्छ । मानिसहरूले त्यस ठाउँमा पहिले कुनै फल्चा थियो भन्ने कुरा नै बिर्सेर नुग: दबू (डबली) भन्न थालेका छन् । यो फल्चा कहिले निर्माण गरिएको थियो भन्ने कुराको कुनै अभिलेख छैन । विसं २०३६ सालतिर यो फल्चा भत्काइएको थियो ।भत्कनुभन्दा अघि यो फल्चा दक्षिणाभिमुख गरी दुई तलाको बनाइएको थियो । फल्चाको छाना झिँगटीले छाएको थियो । माथिल्लो तलामा दक्षिणी मोहडामा तीनवटा सँझ्या:हरू राखिएका थिए भने पश्चिम मोहडामा ठूलो झ्याल राखिएको थियो । फल्चाको पूर्वी मोहडामा पनि एउटा झ्याल बनाइएको थियो । फल्चाको पूर्वी मोहडामा माथि उक्लने भर्‍याङ्ग राखिएको थियो । भुइँतलामा तीनवटा कवल बनाइएका थिए । पश्चिमपट्टिको कवलमा सानो पसल राखिएको थियो । बीचको कवलमा लुँ हितितर्फ फर्काइ (दक्षिणाभिमुख) गरी प्वा:स्या:द्य: स्थापना गरिएको थियो । प्वा:स्या:द्य:लाई भित्तामा टाँसिने गरी नराखी देवता र भित्ताको बीचमा केही खाली ठाउँ छोडेर स्थापना गरिएको थियो । ठूलो पेट भएका प्वा:स्या:द्य:को मूर्तिमा कुनै वस्त्र लगाइएको थिएन, मूर्ति नाङ्गै थियो । पूर्वपट्टिको कवल चाहिँ खाली नै छोडिएको थियो । प्वा:स्या:द्य:को बारेमा एउटा किम्वदन्ती रहेको छ । बेलाबेलामा प्वा:स्या:द्य: फल्चाबाट निस्केर सामुन्ने रहेको लुँ हितिमा पानी खान जान्थे । लुँ हितिमा तीनवटा लहरै रहेका टुटीमध्ये पूर्व र पश्चिमपट्टिको टुटीलाई हत्केलाले थुनेर बीचमा रहेको टुटीबाट पानी खाने गर्थे । कसैलाई पेट दुखेको छ भने फल्चामा स्थापना गरिएको यस देवताको नाभीमा छोएर पूजा गरी लुँ हितिको पानी खाएमा निको हुने विश्वास गरिन्थ्यो (Personal communication: Resident from Tvāye Bāhāḥ, Śākya, male, age 65) ।यो फल्चा भत्काइनुको पछाडि एउटा घटना रहेको छ । पहिले यो फल्चाको माथिल्लो तलामा पुलिस चौकी राखिएको थियो । नुग: टोलमा रहेका युवाहरूको छिमेकी टोलका युवाहरूसँग झैझगडा भइरहन्थ्यो । विसं २०३६ सालतिर त्यसरी नै छिमेकी टोलसँग झगडा हुँदा प्रहरीले झगडा गर्ने युवाहरूलाई समातेर यसै फल्चाको माथि रहेको चौकीमा राखिएको थियो । आफ्नो टोलबासी युवाहरूलाई समातेपछि उत्तेजित भीडले चौकी तोडफोड गरेको थियो । फलस्वरूप पुलिस चौकी त्यहाँबाट हटाएर लुँ हितिको दक्षिणमा रहेको फल्चामा सारिएको थियो । पुलिस चौकी हटेपछि फल्चाको मर्मत गरिएन र बिस्तारै जीर्ण भइ भत्कियो (Personal communication: A resident from Yanāmugaḥ, male, age 45) ।यस फल्चामा चंकि टोलका चिपालु (श्रेष्ठ) हरूको गुठी पनि थियो । अहिले उक्त गुठी पनि बन्द भइसकेको छ । फल्चामा रहेको प्वा:स्या:द्य: अहिले कहाँ छ, गुठी कसरी र कहिले मनाइन्थ्यो भन्ने जानकारी उपलब्ध हुनसकेन ।

historical_events.event_name: Politically motivated damage of the Phalcā
historical_events.event_description: The Phalcā was damaged in 1979, and since then has been turned into an elevated open space.This important Phalcā was located in the heart of Sundhara Patan. It was occupied by a local police station before it was vandalised in 1978-9. The youths of Nugaḥ Ṭola used to hold regular gang fights with the youths from neighbouring quarters in this area. One such fight took place in 1978-9. The local police arrested the youths involved in the gang fight and detained them in the Phalcā building itself An aggressive group of local people attacked the police office, demanding the release of the detainees. After this incident, the local police station was moved to another Phalcā located to the west of Lũ Hiti. Pvāḥsyāḥ Phalcā was abandoned completely and was no longer maintained (source: a resident of Yanāmugaḥ, male, age 45). Though the Phalcā had aguṭhī(established by Cipālus (Śreṣṭha) of Caṃki Ṭola), this group no longer exists today. The idol of Pvāḥsyāḥdyaḥ is also no longer present; it appears that the statue of this deity was stolen and never replaced.

Pvāḥsyāḥ Phalcā was one of fourphalcāsselected for the first PhotoKathmandu Festival in 2015 and became a major success among locals and passers-by. Positioned at a main road in Patan, it became a spectacular object of attention during the days of the festival. Many people articulated the desire to hold on to it and for it to stay beyond the festival time. The Pvāḥsyaḥ Phalcā (Pāṭī) at Sundhara was removed in the 1970s and has stood as platform since then. Art students from Kathmandu University's Art and Design Centre were involved in the PhotoKathmandu project and studied its previous form through old postcards, and conversations with locals before reconstructing it. The aim of the reconstruction was to encourage future perspectives on the post-earthquake city, referencing what has been lost, but also what can be gained again, and how important the ‘institution’ of thepatican be in this context.
